name: Ashwaraj
summary: Raj Comics' half-man, half-horse Suryavanshi prince of Ashwalok, a sword-and-shield warrior with five horses that each hold one power.
origin: In the comics, Ashwaraj is a warrior prince of the Suryavanshi line from the fictional world of Ashwalok, where human-horses live. He is half man and half horse, and he fights evil with a sword and shield and with five horses that each hold a special power. This is a fictional comic warrior, not a figure of mythology.
creators: Pratap Mullick (named by Indianetzone; Comicsbyte credits him with the watercolour covers of the 2024 reissue)

firstAppearance.title: Ashwaraj's first comic
firstAppearance.issue: 1992, Rs 6, with a free sticker; announced by an in-comic ad (per Comicsbyte)

powers: Five horses with one power each

gossip.text: The first ad promised a free Ashwaraj sticker with the six-rupee comic, which Comicsbyte says was all a 1990s kid needed.
The 1992 debut date rests on a single Comicsbyte article, so other sources may differ.
Many of his titles start with the Hindi word for horse, such as Ashwmani, Ashwkhor, Ashwanad and Ashwbaaz.
Ashwaraj is a figure from Hindu mythology.
gossip.truth: He is a fictional Raj Comics warrior; the sources describe an invented world, Ashwalok.

quiz.q: What world does Ashwaraj come from?
quiz.why: He is a prince of Ashwalok, a world of human-horses.

quiz.q: Which of his horses understands any language?
quiz.why: Ashwavat talks with the human-horses, understands any language and relays the others' thoughts.
Tutabuta is the evil magician of Ashwalok. The other three are his commander, sister and beloved.

quiz.q: How many special horses does he have?
quiz.why: He has five horses, each with one power.

quiz.q: What nickname does Ashwaraj earn after breaking Tutabuta's talisman?
quiz.why: He broke the dangerous talisman and claimed the treasure, earning the name Tilism Ka Khiladi, the Talisman Player.

theme.tagline: A horse-prince with five gifted steeds.

facts.text: Ashwaraj is a half-man, half-horse warrior prince of the Suryavanshi line who comes from Ashwalok, a fictional world of human-horses.
He was Raj Comics' second hero built on an animal or creature, after Nagraj, and like Nagraj he is a shape-shifter.
In that first ad he is billed as the winner of a chariot marathon, a victory that won him the affection of Princess Kudumchhumbi.
Tutabuta built a dangerous talisman to seize Ashwalok, but Ashwaraj broke it and claimed the treasure, earning the name Tilism Ka Khiladi, the Talisman Player.
His five horses talk through Ashwavat: the others pass their thoughts to it and it relays them to Ashwaraj, and the link also works in the other direction.
A December 2024 reprint set ends with Hum Paanch, We Five, and follows Ashwaraj searching for his missing companions, the Panchashwa, who vanished in Kalyug.
He teamed up with Bhokal and Gojo in the Khalnayak and Mahanayak crossovers, where the heroes faced a shared villain.
Each of his five horses has one gift: Ashwavat understands any language, Raktambar has far sight, Kalakhor has a keen sense of smell, Shravyashakti hears sharply and Neelkanth analyses.
Comicsbyte calls him an ichchhadhari ashwamanav, a shape-shifting horse-man, and compares him to the shape-shifting snake heroes of the films Nagin and Nagina.
His sister is Ghodilekha, his trusted senapati is Ghudak, and Kudumchhumbi is his beloved, according to Indianetzone.
Comicsbyte says readers liked Ashwaraj in the Sarvanayak series, which was left unfinished and has not been concluded.
One title in his collected lists, Mara Gaya Ashwaraj, means Ashwaraj Has Died, and it sits right before Hum Paanch in the Edition 3 line-up.
ThePrint says Raj Comics sales began falling by 1998, and Comicsbyte says Ashwaraj faded from print a few years after his 1992 start.
Indianetzone lists 29 Raj Comics titles for Ashwaraj, from Karu Ka Khajana and Tilism Ka Khiladi to Hum Paanch, so he carried a long-running series of his own.
All five of his horses got a solo issue named after them: Ashwavat, Kalakhor, Neelkanth, Shravyashakti and Raktambar are each a title in the Raj Comics run.
The August 2026 Combined Edition 2 packs 12 stories into 390 hardcover pages at Rs 1799, with an MDF standee and bookmark, and ends with Ashwasamrat Ashwaraj.
Combined Edition 3 opens with Main Hoon Khalnayak (I Am the Villain) and follows it with a title about Tutabuta's soul, hinting the magician lingers after defeat.
The December 2024 General Set 2 sells 32-page comics at Rs 100 each and adds a free poster, with covers in the watercolour style of the late Pratap Mullick.
Two of his titles are Ashwaraj aur Main and Ashwaraj aur Tum, meaning Ashwaraj and Me and Ashwaraj and You, which sit in Combined Edition 2.
In January 2024 Raj Comics by Sanjay Gupta took pre-orders for a 64-page two-in-one Ashwaraj and Bankelal book at Rs 400, bundled with a Bheriya book and a free standee for Rs 600.

timeline.note: Raj Comics by Manoj Gupta reprints a set ending in Hum Paanch, in December 2024.

timeline.note: In August 2026 Combined Editions 2 and 3 are announced as 390-page hardcovers, beside matching Gojo books.

kidSummary: Ashwaraj is a half-man, half-horse prince from the made-up world of Ashwalok. He fights with a sword and shield and has five special horses, each with its own gift, and he is a fictional comic hero, not a figure from mythology.
